items.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014
items.q: I heard Barry Harris in person and the old bebop players. Oh. This is jazz.

ctx.x: Because in Japan I was listening to bebop records, just old recordings, just two minutes or three minutes, and maybe a good line, but no bass solo, no drum solo. But I didn’t know that it was because of the limitations of the recording. But I thought that was bebop. So that’s why I came to New York, ’82, and I heard for the first time Barry Harris. Now he played like a five minute, ten minute solo, and go to the drum solo, bass solo, and interplay with each other. Oh. Wow. This is what I played with the fusion,…

Right. Because that music was about — well it was only about twenty years old — well no, more like thirty I guess in 1980. Bebop being the late ‘40’s and early ‘50’s. Yeah. But that’s really interesting about the recording technology and how it limited the players.
